settings.threads: one consumer per data shard, each its own thread
settings.barrier: `_durable` writes: a settle and its fsync each (RFC 0072)

notes: Every collection op is one apply batch. The durable row writes through the `_durable` operations, one fsync per batch; the relaxed row through the standard ones, one fsync per elapsed window (RFC 0072), the counterpart of the others' relaxed knobs.
Retains every superseded version; the other systems retain none. Read the update row beside the footprint, never alone.
Barrier count is not recorded: PageStore exposes no public IoCounts accessor and RFC 0060 forbids changing a shipped crate.

Multi: 3 consumers, each its own thread owning one data shard and one `Thing` collection on it; row n is consumer n % 3's. A collection is indivisible (its chains belong to its owner), so the dataset is split by owner, as a node splits its owners across workers. Every data shard writes through one storage shard (RFC 0073).

Measured on the RFC 0065 producer/consumer harness: `wall_ns` is the phase's wall clock, `total_ns` is the sum of the timed windows, and the percentiles are pooled across every consumer. Read counters are absent (phase 4).
